newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends down, gilts up in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends down, gilts up in active trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday at 5.0-5.5 percent, down from Monday's close of 6.25-6.5 percent and dealers said rates would remain around 5.0 percent for the rest of the week.
They said sentiment had improved and liquidity was expected to ease over the coming days on inflows into the banking system through interest payments on government securities.

"Most market players feel call money rates will be around 5.0 percent or even less in the coming days," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "There are good inflows coming in through interest payments and redemption of treasury bills.
ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said in a debt market report inflows into the banking system between May 21 and the end of the month will be in excess of 23 billion rupees.
It said call money was likely to trade between 3.0 percent and 7.0 percent for the rest of May.
Dealers said lower call money rates and expectations of easy liquidity in the immediate future fuelled buying interest in government securities on Tuesday.
They said prices of government securities rose in brisk trade, with market attention mainly focussed in short- and medium-term securities with maturities up to 2002.
"There was some buying interest today as call was easy and there is a feeling that it will remain easy for some time to come," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
"Most of the action was in securities with maturities up to 2002 although the 13.05 percent 2007 was also traded," he said.

Dealers said the 13.05 percent 2007 stock was traded at 101 rupees on Tuesday against its last traded 100.74, the 13.40 percent 1999 rose to 104.75 from 104.55, the 13.50 percent 1997 to 101.96 from 101.83 and the 13.80 percent 2002 to 105.75 from 105.725.
The 12.69 percent 2002 was traded at 100.45 rupees against 100.35.
Dealers said yields on treasury bills fell as buying interest pushed prices up.
Treasury bills maturing in January 1998 yielded 9.05 percent against 9.15 and April bills 9.25 percent against 9.35.
